Il TLT 20Y è sceso dell'1,58% (tassi in rialzo) e il Brent è a -5,28% (oil in forte calo, supporto per equity). Con questi dati il sentiment resta leggermente negativo, con un punteggio di 3/10.
sentiment.reason_en: The VIX at 15.18 (down) points to a defensive market without panic; the S&P 500 is down -0.76% and the DXY is flat at 101.10, indicating pressure on risk assets. The 20‑year TLT fell 1.58% (rising rates) and Brent is down -5.28% (oil sharply lower, equity‑supportive). These numbers keep sentiment modestly negative, yielding a score of 3/10.

Commodities: Brent -5,28% (oil spike, bearish per inflazione) mentre l'oro è stabile (+0,03%) con trend "mixed". Valute: EUR/USD -0,56% e DXY stabile a 101,10, suggerendo pressione sul dollaro ma senza trend netto.

audio_narrative_it.text: La chiusura del nuovo fronte di guerra nello Yemen aumenta le preoccupazioni di approvvigionamento, contribuendo al calo del Brent. audio_narrative_it.text: Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

audio_narrative_it.title: Criptovalute
audio_narrative_it.text: Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si muove in calo, scendendo del 2,96%, con un flusso ETF netto di +3,8 milioni di dollari. Il prezzo si mantiene sopra gli ottantamila dollari, mentre i rendimenti dei Treasury statunitensi salgono, spingendo gli investitori verso asset più sicuri. Ethereum scende del 2,78% a duemilatrecentounocento dollari, Solana cala del 3,07% a centoventicinque dollari e BNB diminuisce del 2,37% a settecentosettantatré dollari. Questi movimenti indicano una pressione di vendita nei principali altcoin. articles.title: Europe’s Third Way on China
articles.snippet: Instead of choosing between a confrontation with China and business as usual, European policymakers should examine the benefits and costs of trade sector by sector to identify where mutually beneficial arrangements remain possible. Economic modeling shows that pragmatism beats more extreme options in most cases.

articles.title: Hormuz Supply Crisis to Change LNG Market Forever
articles.snippet: The Strait of Hormuz crisis has turned roughly 20% of global LNG supply into something buyers now have to treat as interruptible. Nearly seven months after traffic through the strait collapsed, LNG exports from Qatar and the UAE remain severely constrained. Buyers in Europe and Asia are responding by looking for supply that does not depend on Hormuz at all—from Canada, Mozambique, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea and Argentina—and reconsidering how much of their future gas demand they are willing to tie to a single export route.
